title: Murder Mystery at the Finucane Manor
note: The Hollow Order: player-safe character cards only. The murder plot, blackmail letters, clues and tribunal are still being written (see the host plan document). Nothing here may reveal the murderer.
setting: Hollowmere Manor, Blackthorn Hollow, England · Autumn 1892
background: Twenty-five years ago, eight children from four old families spent their summers together at Hollowmere Manor, running wild through its gardens, its library and the corridors their parents told them never to enter.

Those summers ended suddenly. On the last night of the last summer, a fire swept through the manor's east wing, and a child died in it: Eleanor Vale, the little sister of Silas Vale, then the young under-footman, now the butler who still serves the four families today. The inquest called it a tragic accident. The east wing was sealed, the children were sent home, and nobody ever spoke of that night again.

The eight children grew up, and grew closer in other ways: four of them married the other four. Now Sir Jonathan Pemberwick has inherited Hollowmere from his great-uncle, Lord Edmund Hollowmere, and has invited his oldest friends back to the manor for the first time since that final summer, to celebrate, to reminisce, and to hear his plans for the estate's future.
Formal evening dress is expected. Old friendships will be renewed. Old questions may be asked.

characters.name: Sir Jonathan Reginald Pemberwick
characters.tagline: House Pemberwick · Keeper of the Manor
characters.biography: You have recently inherited Hollowmere Manor from your great-uncle, Lord Edmund, and have invited your old friends back to reconnect and to consider restoring and developing the estate.

relationships.text: Your wife. Sharper than you and politer than you; she has rescued more of your schemes than she lets you know.
Your oldest friend and favourite rival. You have competed at everything since you were boys, and he still disputes who won the great boat race on the Hollowmere lake.
Grant's wife, and the only person alive who can make him lose an argument. You find this deeply entertaining.
He understands your appetite for opportunity better than anyone. A natural partner for the estate plans, if you can trust his numbers.
Nanor's wife: warm, generous and quietly unconvinced by your grander ideas. Winning her support would mean a great deal.
Overly fascinated with the manor's history. You need him enthusiastic about the estate's future, not poking around its sealed rooms.
Griff's wife: practical and hard to impress. If anyone can value the manor's collection honestly, it is her.

objectives: Win support for the estate's future and establish yourself as the natural leader.

card.personality: Charming, bold, persuasive and relentlessly optimistic; occasionally reckless.
card.background: You have recently inherited Hollowmere Manor from your great-uncle, Lord Edmund, and have invited your old friends back to reconnect and to consider restoring and developing the estate.
card.how_met: You turned up at the Ashford midsummer ball in 1884 without an invitation (yours, you insisted, had been lost in the post). Danielle recognised you at once from those Hollowmere summers, covered for you with her mother, and spent the rest of the night pretending not to be amused by you. Six months later you proposed in a box at Covent Garden. She said yes before you had finished the speech you had rehearsed for a week.
card.childhood_memory: You and Grant were wrestling over who got to hold the spirit board when somebody's elbow caught the candelabra. It went over onto the papers. You have always been certain it was Grant's elbow. You have never been entirely certain.
card.motto: Every great fortune begins with someone willing to take a risk.
card.costume: Tailored Victorian evening coat, waistcoat, pocket watch.

characters.name: Lady Danielle Cordelia Pemberwick (née Ashford)
characters.tagline: Ashford bloodline · Keeper of the Covenant
characters.biography: You were raised among families that prized discretion and tradition. You manage society occasions, and sometimes the fallout from Jonathan's ambitions.

relationships.text: Your ambitious husband: charming, bold and occasionally reckless. You manage the consequences more often than he realises.
Jonathan's oldest rival. You have watched the two of them compete since childhood, and you keep the peace when it matters.
You adore her wit. The two of you have shared many a look across a dinner table while your husbands argue.
Charming and calculating. He and Jonathan get along a little too well whenever money is involved.
You value her warmth and her genuine goodness. One of the very few people you trust completely.
Brilliant and dramatic. He asks the questions about those old summers that everyone else has learned not to ask.
You value her practicality. Like you, she prefers facts to theatrics.

objectives: Protect your family's dignity, support the reunion, and discover why the older generation guarded its traditions so closely.

card.occupation: Society hostess and patron of the arts
card.personality: Sophisticated, observant, composed and devastatingly polite.
card.background: You were raised among families that prized discretion and tradition. You manage society occasions, and sometimes the fallout from Jonathan's ambitions.
card.how_met: Jonathan Pemberwick appeared at your family's midsummer ball in 1884 without an invitation. You recognised him instantly, the same boy who once dared everyone to climb Hollowmere's bell tower, and you covered for him with your mother. Six months later he proposed at Covent Garden in the middle of a speech so long you said yes just to save the second act. Your mother, unusually, raised no objection at all.
card.childhood_memory: Eleanor didn't want to go to the séance. You told her that if she refused, you would tell Silas she had stolen your hair ribbons. She came, crying. You have never told a soul why Eleanor was in that room that night.
card.motto: Good manners are simply the most elegant form of control.
card.costume: Elegant late-Victorian evening dress, gloves, understated jewellery.

characters.name: Lord Grant Bartholomew Blackthorne III
characters.tagline: House Blackthorne · Keeper of the Passage
characters.biography: You come from a family that kept the estate's boundaries, maps and routes. You believe you know Hollowmere far better than its new owner does.

relationships.text: Your wife: the rare person who can out-argue you. You would never say so aloud.
Your lifelong rival and oldest friend. He thinks he knows Hollowmere because he owns it. You know it because your family mapped it.
Jonathan's wife: elegant, observant, and far too clever for him.
A rival intellect. You enjoy matching wits with him, and checking his arithmetic.
Kind and principled. She has a way of making you behave better than you intended to.
His wild theories amuse you endlessly. You enjoy dismantling them; he enjoys rebuilding them.
Griff's wife. You both respect evidence, which makes her far more dangerous in an argument than her husband.

objectives: Protect Blackthorne interests and establish the real boundaries and history of the estate.

card.personality: Precise, competitive, arrogant in a charming way, and loyal to the friends he chooses.
card.background: You come from a family that kept the estate's boundaries, maps and routes. You believe you know Hollowmere far better than its new owner does.
card.how_met: In 1885 you attended Caroline's lecture at the Royal Botanic Society (not entirely by chance) and challenged her findings from the floor. She took your argument apart in front of two hundred people. You asked her to dinner to 'continue the discussion'. You have been continuing it ever since; you married the following spring.
card.childhood_memory: You were the only one who knew the secret passage behind the library, so you led everyone into the east wing. Then you wedged a chair under the records-room door so no grown-up could walk in on you. When the fire started, everyone fled down your passage in single file, in the dark. Eleanor was the smallest, and she was furthest from it.
card.motto: I am not arguing. I am explaining why you are mistaken.
card.costume: Structured Victorian suit, measuring tools or a rolled map.

characters.name: Lady Caroline Evangeline Blackthorne (née Whitmore)
characters.tagline: Whitmore bloodline · Keeper of the Garden
characters.biography: You spent your childhood afternoons in the manor's gardens and later pursued rare and unconventional botanical specimens.

relationships.text: Your husband: brilliant and exhausting. You still win most of your arguments.
Grant's lifelong rival. Charming, impulsive, and always selling something.
You love her humour: dry, quick and perfectly polite.
Always alert to a deal. You have learned to keep your research notes well out of his sight.
Her warmth is genuine, and you treasure it.
You share his curiosity about Hollowmere's old plants and older histories. He is the one person who never finds your specimens strange.
Practical, sceptical and excellent company. The two of you get along famously.

objectives: Learn what happened to the gardens, and preserve your research.

card.personality: Independent, sharp-witted, curious and thoroughly unimpressed by pomp.
card.background: You spent your childhood afternoons in the manor's gardens and later pursued rare and unconventional botanical specimens.
card.how_met: In 1885 a pompous surveyor stood up at your Royal Botanic Society lecture and announced that your soil maps were wrong. It was Grant Blackthorne, the boy who used to trample your seedlings at Hollowmere. You took his argument apart in front of two hundred people, and he asked you to dinner to 'continue the discussion'. You said yes mostly so you could win. You married the following spring.
card.childhood_memory: You smuggled a bottle of your father's surgical spirit into the séance, because Griff's book said it would make the candles burn blue. You poured it into a saucer on the desk. When the candles went over, the spirit went up in a sheet of flame. You were nine years old, and you knew exactly what was in that bottle.
card.motto: Nature is rarely cruel without a reason. People are another matter.
card.costume: Botanical brooch, dark green gown, pressed-flower notebook.

characters.name: Baron Nanor Percival Ravenscroft
characters.tagline: House Ravenscroft · Keeper of the Treasury
characters.biography: You were raised to manage fortunes, and you have always been fascinated by the strange traditions attached to inherited wealth.

relationships.text: Your perceptive wife. She sees through you more often than you would like, and she worries about your risks.
A potential partner. He has the manor; you understand money. Together, the possibilities are considerable.
Jonathan's wife: composed and impossible to read. You suspect she is the real negotiator in that marriage.
A rival intellect. You enjoy sparring with him, and you never let him near your ledgers.
Grant's wife: sharp and entirely immune to your charm. A rare challenge.
He shares your curiosity about the occult and the strange traditions of old families.
Griff's wife. She knows what things are really worth, which makes her useful, and dangerous, at a negotiating table.

objectives: Determine the estate's true value, and keep Ravenscroft influence over the fortune.

card.personality: Charming, calculating, comfortable with risk and always alert to a deal.
card.background: You were raised to manage fortunes, and you have always been fascinated by the strange traditions attached to inherited wealth.
card.how_met: In 1886 Taylor held a charity auction for a children's hospital. You bid an outrageous sum for a truly dreadful painting of a horse, partly to impress her and partly because you cannot resist winning. She thanked you sweetly, then talked you into funding an entire new ward. You have never closed a worse deal, or a better one. You married the following summer.
card.childhood_memory: You were the lookout at the far end of the passage. You saw the first flames, and you ran: not to the grown-ups, but to your own room, where you climbed into bed and pretended to be asleep. If you had shouted, the adults would have come five minutes sooner. You have done the arithmetic many times.
card.motto: Everything has a price. The trick is discovering who is willing to pay it.
card.costume: Rich waistcoat, signet ring, a ledger or an antique coin.

characters.name: Lady Taylor Beatrice Ravenscroft (née Bellamy)
characters.tagline: Bellamy bloodline · Keeper of the Flame
characters.biography: You are known for supporting schools and hospitals, and you grew up hearing that wealth requires duty and sacrifice.

relationships.text: Your husband. His risk-taking worries you; his charm still works on you, which worries you more.
Ambitious and persuasive. You would like to believe his plans for the estate will do some good.
You admire her competence. She is the person you would call in a crisis.
Proud and clever, but loyal underneath it all, if he has chosen you as a friend.
Her humour is a delight; she makes every evening feel shorter.
Endlessly enthusiastic. His stories of the old summers bring back memories you had half forgotten.
You value her steadiness. When everyone else panics, Grace does not.

objectives: Reconnect the group, and advocate for using the inheritance responsibly.

card.personality: Warm, socially adept, principled but not naive.
card.background: You are known for supporting schools and hospitals, and you grew up hearing that wealth requires duty and sacrifice.
card.how_met: In 1886 you organised a charity auction for a children's hospital, and Nanor Ravenscroft bid a ridiculous sum for the worst painting in the room, a lopsided horse. Afterwards you persuaded him to fund a whole new ward as well. He still claims it was his idea. You married the following summer.
card.childhood_memory: You were the keeper of the candles. You lit every one of them, more than a dozen, crowded together on the old desk among the papers, because it looked so beautiful in the dark. Nanny had told you a hundred times never to leave a flame beside paper. You have always told yourself that someone else knocked them over, so it couldn't have been your fault.
card.motto: Wealth means very little if one has nothing worthwhile to do with it.
card.costume: Elegant jewel-toned gown, with a candle or charity-ribbon motif.

characters.name: Professor Griffin Thaddeus Wraithmore
characters.tagline: House Wraithmore · Keeper of the Records
characters.biography: You study ancient civilisations, hidden societies and unexplained events. Your family's records tie you to Blackthorn Hollow.

relationships.text: Your wife. She keeps you grounded and demands proof for everything, which makes her approval worth having.
He owns the manor you have longed to explore since you were a boy. Stay on his good side.
Jonathan's wife: gracious, and she watches everything. You suspect she remembers more of those summers than she says.
He debates every theory you have ever had. You secretly enjoy it.
A fellow lover of forgotten things. She found the strangest plants in those gardens.
He shares your fascination with the occult. Possibly the only one who takes your theories seriously.
Kind and patient; she listens to your stories longer than anyone else.

objectives: Investigate the fire, locate the lost records, and make a historic discovery.

card.personality: Eccentric, brilliant, dramatic, and wildly excitable about forgotten history.
card.background: You study ancient civilisations, hidden societies and unexplained events. Your family's records tie you to Blackthorn Hollow.
card.how_met: In 1887, in a gallery of the British Museum, you were explaining (loudly) to a small crowd why a carved stone was a genuine Druidic relic. A woman in the crowd calmly informed you it was a forgery from the 1840s. It was Grace Sinclair, whom you had last seen hiding from you in Hollowmere's library. You argued for three hours. The next morning you returned with flowers and a twelve-page rebuttal. She read both. You married the following year.
card.childhood_memory: The night of the fire was your idea. You had read about a séance in one of your father's forbidden books, and you dared the others to hold one in the locked records room of the east wing. When little Eleanor Vale said she was frightened, you called her a baby until she came along. You have spent twenty-five years telling yourself it was only a game.
card.motto: The absence of evidence is often merely evidence that someone has hidden it.
card.costume: Tweed Victorian suit, spectacles, notebook, an old book.

characters.name: Lady Grace Ophelia Wraithmore (née Sinclair)
characters.tagline: Sinclair bloodline · Keeper of the Relics
characters.biography: You are an expert in authenticating rare artefacts, and you much prefer physical proof to your husband's dramatic supernatural theories.

relationships.text: Your husband: brilliant but distractible. You love him; you also check his sources.
The new owner of Hollowmere, and of its collection. You would very much like to see it.
You respect her judgement. She never wastes a word.
Arrogant, but he respects evidence. That makes him tolerable.
You enjoy her company enormously, and her refusal to be impressed by anyone.
He will want to know what everything is worth. You would rather know where it came from.
Warm and steady; you are very fond of her.

objectives: Assess the manor's collection, and protect the provenance of important relics.

card.personality: Practical, sceptical, independent and quietly observant.
card.background: You are an expert in authenticating rare artefacts, and you much prefer physical proof to your husband's dramatic supernatural theories.
card.how_met: In 1887 you were consulting at the British Museum when a man in tweed began lecturing a crowd about a 'genuine Druidic relic'. You informed him it was an 1840s forgery. It was Griffin Wraithmore, the boy who once chased you round Hollowmere's library with a 'cursed' book. You argued for three hours. He came back the next morning with flowers and a twelve-page rebuttal. The rebuttal was wrong; the flowers were lovely. You married the following year.
card.childhood_memory: You were the last one into the passage. Behind you, through the smoke, you heard Eleanor calling your name. You did not go back. Afterwards you told everyone the room was already full of fire. It wasn't.
card.motto: Extraordinary claims are considerably more interesting when accompanied by proof.
card.costume: Refined Victorian dress, cameo, a magnifying glass or an artefact sketch.

remember: What do I remember about the night of the fire?
What do I remember about the east wing?

Have you been to the east wing tonight?
